title: Review of c27's SIBRM motile-repair claim: repair replicates on fresh seeds 10-11 (6/6 front cuts re-close the ring by +100-160, one from closure 0.25), but no repaired cell swims 3 body lengths afterwards (0.45-2.67 BL), and M is the per-body label drive
summary: c27's twinrepair.py (wound substrate kept, 40% front cut at t=10000, exact branched twins, 2500 steps) on new seeds 10 and 11, 3 cells each, and c27's motion.py. All 6 cut cells survive, re-close their link ring (closure 0.25-0.57 -> >= 0.9 at +100-160) and hold ring score >= 1.5 in every later frame; as in my earlier review the remnant first contracts to 10-40% of pre-cut area and then regrows (back at +360 to +2400). After repair (+340 to the first split, merge or loss) cut cells move 0.45-2.67 body lengths, twins 0.10-3.52; none of the 6 repaired cells reaches 3 BL. A labkit pack on seed 12 shows ringed cells from noise (L membrane-like in 116/172 individuals, aggregate rim/core 1.49) but its --damage fell back to a 6x-median merged cluster, so it says nothing about repair of a mature cell.

verdicts.limitation: R replicates (with my earlier review, 11 of 12 cuts on seeds 8-11 repair, including ones with no substrate at the wound), but repair is contraction to a 10-40% ringed remnant and regrowth. The claim's SIBRM needs the same individuals to swim on: on my 6 cells none reaches 3 BL after repair, so R and M together are 3 of 23 cuts across c27's and my seeds. M comes from the label drive, which gives each labelled body one rigid velocity (the mean substrate gradient over the body), an operator per individual in the code. The closure <= 0.26 death threshold does not hold strictly (seed 10 cell 13 repaired from 0.25).
